| Meeting | Session B leaves you with |
|:---|:---|
| **1** &nbsp;Finding a question | Five candidate questions, filtered — one of which becomes the project |
| **2** &nbsp;Causal language | Your team's ground rules, and a diagnosed causal graph |
| **3** &nbsp;Models and uncertainty | The overclaim your own project is most at risk of making |
| **4** &nbsp;How inference fails | The one threat your design will have to survive |
| **5** &nbsp;Controls and matching | Which back doors you can close, and with what data |
| **6** &nbsp;Writing the problem | Your problem statement, as an outline |
| **7** &nbsp;Research designs I | Whether an experiment, instrument or discontinuity is open to you |
| **8** &nbsp;Research designs II | Your design defended in public, plus the attack that landed — the identification section and the limitation |
| **9** &nbsp;Measurement and data | Your key variable, operationalised, and what data the design demands |
| **10** &nbsp;Getting the data | Your data source, access route, timeline and plan B — the memo |
| **11** &nbsp;Midterm and using data | Your own data, interrogated, and what is wrong with it |
| **12** &nbsp;Seeing the data | The one figure your project lives or dies on |
| **13** &nbsp;Writing the design paper | The whole paper, as a sketch, marked up by somebody else |
